title: Validation of Novel, Accelerated, and Artifact-Resistant Techniques for Whole-Body Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Children
summary: Durch neue technische Entwicklungen und hochmoderne MRT-Geräte ist es heute grundsätzlich möglich, die Messzeit der Kernspintomographie bei bestimmten MRT-Untersuchungen deutlich zu reduzieren. Ziel der Studie ist es zu untersuchen, ob die mit der neuen Technik aufgenommenen Bilder eine vergleichbare Bildqualität und diagnostische Aussagekraft wie die Standarduntersuchung erreichen.

interventions.name:
All patients referred for an MRI examination in the
Pediatrics Department, regardless of the (suspected) diagnosis or
clinical presentation, for whom no exclusion criteria apply,
should be included in the analysis. After informed consent has been obtained, experimental sequences will be acquired

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Male and female patients
Referrals from pediatrics with a clinical indication for an MRI scan
Written consent to participate in the study from the patient and/or legal guardian
No need for anesthesia or sedation for the examination
Exclusion criteria:
All MRI-related exclusion criteria
Patient non-compliance with MRI examination requirements.
The need for anesthesia or sedation for the examination.
Lack of written consent to the study from the patient and/or legal guardian, or explicit refusal by younger children (generally < 12 years of age)
